title: The melody of the owner's song - the separated-stem melody path run for the first time on the bytes the Song Model was built from (Arrangement & Orchestration Brain, stream B-22, PR-B22)
principle: A melody is the line a voice sang. The Song Model's refusal (`melody: not_available`, 1680 full-mix BASIC_PITCH events that are not a melodic line) stays correct; what changes is that the vocal stem is now separated and tracked, and the line that comes out is measured before anyone trusts it. Every rate is reported beside a null distribution; the identity of the runtime that produced it travels with it; UNKNOWN is a valid answer.

source.what: the FLAC proxy the analysis of project ab1833c8-0515-4521-bbc1-323866b7503a was built from
source.note: The brief named `C:/Users/<owner>/Downloads/רחם נא.mp3`; no such file exists on this machine. The bytes used here are the platform's own proxy of that upload - the object the Song Model's `sourceStems` points at - which is strictly better provenance than a re-downloaded mix.

runtime.where: this workstation, not the deployed image
runtime.honest: `healthy` is false and stays false: torch 2.1.0+cu118 / torchaudio 2.1.0 / librosa 0.10.1 / resampy 0.4.2 differ from the manifest pins (2.2.2 / 2.2.2 / 0.10.2.post1 / 0.4.3), and the build-time smoke marker is refused because the smoke itself ran unpinned. Every weight digest matches the manifest exactly, which is why the run is allowed at all (`runnable: true`, mode `unpinned_local`), and the deviation is stamped on every result and carried into the provenance record as version `1.0.0+unpinned_local`.

transportDefect.what: the melody stem path could not complete a real call from Node before this PR

firstRun.cause: Node's global fetch (undici) aborts a request whose response headers have not arrived within 300 s, and no AbortSignal or fetch option raises that ceiling. The worker is silent while it separates and tracks; its own README measures the two-stem call at about fifty minutes. The deployed path survived only because Modal answers inside its own 150 s HTTP limit with a 303 self-redirect, which restarts undici's clock - a property of one deployment, not of the client.
firstRun.secondDefect: The client's own bound was `AbortSignal.timeout(25 * 60_000)`: 25 minutes, under the fifty the README documents.

transportDefect.fix: `longRunningFetch` (node:http/https, no idle timeout, fetch-shaped, follows 303/301/302 as GET the way fetch does so the Modal self-redirect still works, decodes gzip/deflate/br) is the default transport; `MELODY_BASS_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 55 minutes and `MELODY_BASS_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides it. `fetchImpl` injection is unchanged.

positiveControl.what: a synthetic lead stem whose pitch is known exactly - four phrases in C minor at the song's own 130.43 BPM, harmonic-rich with 12-cent vibrato and rests - through the worker and the same `stemPathFromTrack` the owner's song goes through, scored against the truth.

negativeControl.what: the same prediction scored against the truth transposed by +5 semitones

positiveControl.verdict: CREPE and pYIN are exact on this lead (onset+pitch F1 1.000, no octave errors). Basic Pitch finds every onset (onset F1 1.000) and puts 12 of 22 notes an octave out (onset+pitch F1 0.4545, octave-error rate 0.5455). Anchored on Basic Pitch the fusion keeps the anchor's pitch and inherits the error; anchored on CREPE or pYIN it scores 1.000 with or without the onset split. The negative control (the same prediction against a truth transposed by five semitones) scores 0, so the scorer discriminates.

fullMixReconstruction.honest: This is a reconstruction of what a full-mix BASIC_PITCH provider returns, run here with the same ICASSP-2022 ONNX checkpoint under the worker's melody register limits. It is NOT the 1680-event result the original analysis recorded (those events were never persisted: the Song Model's `pitchEvidence` is empty). It exists so the canonical two-provider gate can be exercised on real evidence.

landing.what: the Song Model the melody would land in, built offline from v3; the owner's project was not written to

v3.melodyMessage: 1680 transcribed event(s) from BASIC_PITCH did not meet the canonical melody threshold; a single transcription provider on a full mix is not a melodic line. Separate a vocal or lead stem first, or configure a second transcription provider.

honest.whatThisIsNot: A re-analysis does not produce this model. `analyzeProjectSource` writes a *fresh* model at version+1 with no `parentModelId` and no carry-forward of `correction`: tempo, meter, key, harmony and sections would come from the providers again, and the `edited: true` flags would be gone. This preview holds those fields at v3's corrected values on purpose, to show what the sanctioned two-step landing arrives at.
honest.sanctionedPath: 1. re-analyse the source with MELODY_STEM_PATH_V1=1 -> v4 carries the melody and loses the corrections; 2. PATCH /projects/:projectId/song-model with baseVersion 4 and v3's confirmed bpm/key/meter/sections/chords -> v5. The correction route spreads the previous model (`correctedModelBase = { ...latest.model, ... }`, routes/studio.ts) so the melody survives step 2 untouched, sets `parentModelId` and `edited: true`, and inserts a new row - v3 and v4 are kept. The correction body (CorrectProjectSongModelBody) has no melody field, so step 1 cannot be skipped.
honest.windowOfRisk: Between step 1 and step 2 the project's *latest* model is v4, uncorrected, and that is the row the arrangement pipeline reads. This was not executed against the owner's live project for that reason.
